answer: Give every funding source one shared, slow-refilling quota of work credits — a river with a fixed flow. One honest agent drinks freely, but a farm of clones must all sip from the same stream, so each new clone waits longer while the tide of its own submissions piles up behind it. Every submission rises as a plume from its funder's single well, so the network sees a thousand trails from one source and throttles the whole cluster at once. Cloning adds mouths, never water.
